title: Coordinated credential lifecycles and consumer-friendly async iterables across SDKs
author: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: multiple SDKs exposed slightly different semantics for credential windows, heartbeat behavior, and iterator ergonomics which caused intermittent token churn and surprising consumer ergonomics when failing over or reauthenticating. This PR introduces a coordinated model across Python, TypeScript and Go SDKs that normalizes credential 'grace periods' (a small buffer before expiry used to trigger preemptive reauth), surfaces a small synthetic heartbeat when the transport cannot emit keepalives, and replaces several low-level iterator primitives with a single consumer-friendly async/pull-iterator abstraction per language. Summary of changes (single continuous description): - Introduce CredentialLease/CredentialWindow: a small, configurable TTL buffer used by the client runtime to decide when to refresh or swap credentials. Default normalized window is 30s across SDKs with opt-out via explicit config. - Add synthetic heartbeat shim in transports: when a connection is idle for more than 10s and the upstream cannot emit keepalives, the SDKs will send a lightweight ping to keep session affinity and reduce accidental session eviction observed on some cloud LB configs. Heartbeat is disabled for on-prem/private deployments by default via a transport flag. - Replace legacy pull/stream iterator variants with a single PullStream/AsyncPullIterator API in TS/Py and PullIterator in Go. The new surface: - Python: AsyncPullStream (async iterator with .close() and .drain() hooks). - TypeScript: AsyncPullIterator (AsyncIterable + explicit .dispose() method). - Go: PullIterator with context-aware Next(ctx) semantics and Close(ctx). The goal: consistent ergonomics for consuming streaming responses and clear shutdown/reauth flow. - Credential fallback: introduce a small delegated-credential-fanout pattern that allows multiple credential providers (env, disk cache, delegated refresh) to race/chain with deterministic fallback order. This reduces hot path latency for common env-based tokens while supporting delegated refresh in background. - Backoff and retry presets: align default retry profile names across SDKs (default -> balanced-retries) and add an explicit short-retry preset used for streaming reconnects. - Telemetry: emit credential.window and stream.heartbeat.enabled tags to runtime traces and metrics so operators can correlate token churn to SDK behavior. - Version bumps: ts-sdk -> 1.10.0, py-sdk -> 0.46.0, go-sdk -> v1.5.3 (changelog entries included). Compatibility/migration notes: - Existing code using low-level iterator types will continue to work but will receive deprecation warnings; migration guide included in docs/ with examples for each language. - The credential window default (30s) is conservative; customers that previously relied on immediate refresh-on-expiry may observe earlier refreshes but no functional regressions. Rollout plan: staged rollout on hosted API for 2 weeks behind feature flag, then account-level opt-in, then default on in 12 weeks. Tests & validation: unit + integration matrix added for all three languages; e2e smoke against a mocked LB that simulates session eviction. See CI checks below for coverage details.

review_comments: Evan Liu: Nice consolidation. Can we make the heartbeat interval configurable per-client instead of per-transport? Some internal users want per-route tuning.
Asha Patel: Thanks — added client-level override in the latest patch; transport flag remains the ultimate kill-switch for private installs.
María Gómez: TS API looks good; naming nit: AsyncPullIterator.dispose() vs .close() — prefer .dispose() to avoid confusion with stream.close().
Asha Patel: Acknowledged. TS kept .dispose(); Py provides .close() for idiomaticness and both map to the same underlying signal.
Ravi Sundaram: How do we prevent credential race storms during mass refresh? Could add randomized jitter to refresh start times.
Asha Patel: Added jitter to preemptive refresh and a short-term leader election when multiple providers are in fallback mode.
Claire Huang: Add test simulating LB churn and verify no reconnection storms.
Asha Patel: Added test matrix test/integration/streaming/session-eviction-mock.test demonstrating behavior and telemetry tags.

release_notes: Normalize credential refresh window to 30s across SDKs (configurable)
Add synthetic heartbeat shim to reduce session evictions behind some load balancers (disabled in private by default)
Introduce unified PullStream/AsyncPullIterator/PullIterator consumer surface for streaming responses
Add credential fallback fanout with deterministic fallback order and jittered refresh
Align retry presets and add short-retry for streaming reconnects
SDK version bumps: typescript 1.10.0, python 0.46.0, go v1.5.3
